walkthroughs.body_html: Albert Dock derelict by 1981 Toxteth riots; Tate Liverpool opened 1988. Capital of Culture 2008 attracted £750 million investment, 9.7 million extra visitors. Lost UNESCO status 2021 over Liverpool Waters development. Population still below 1930s peak but growing.

Manchester Ship Canal redundant by 1980; redevelopment from 1985. Lowry Centre 2000; Imperial War Museum North 2002; MediaCity UK 2007 (BBC + ITV, 4400+ jobs). Local employment rates rose. Some original residents feel disconnected from new opportunities.

Shoreditch transformed since 2000: house prices rose from £150000 to £900000+. Original Bengali community displaced. Coventry Climax site in Heygate redeveloped Elephant & Castle: 1200 social homes demolished, 82 social replacements. Regeneration creates winners and losers.

mcqs.q: Liverpool was European Capital of Culture in:

options: Gentrification is when the government rebuilds an old part of the city.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Gentrification means the city becomes more polluted as it grows.
The process by which wealthier residents move into a previously low-income urban area, raising property prices and often displacing original residents.

mcqs.q: What is the main social impact of gentrification?
options: Displacement of long-term lower-income residents as rents and property prices rise, often along with loss of community businesses and cultural identity — even if the area looks 'improved'.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Gentrification only has positive effects because it makes areas nicer.
Gentrification means evicting all residents by force.

Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
